# Overview

**Module 1: Import and QC**

This module handles:

1. Finding and importing sequencing files (BAM, FASTQ, FASTA)
2. Detecting PacBio HiFi BAMs and summarising their pass count (np) and read quality (rq)
3. Optional filters, each applied only when switched on: minimum PacBio pass count (`np_min`), duplicate read names (`check_duplicate_readnames`), downsampling (`downsample`) and adapter trimming (`trim`)
4. Read length and base quality per sample

**Outputs:**

- `01_import_qc/qc.xlsx` – file details, per-sample read counts at each step, read length and quality, PacBio summaries
- `01_import_qc/plots/` – the figures in this report
- `module_data/01_import_qc.RData` – the reads passed to Module 2

**Settings for this run:** np filter `r ifelse(is.na(params$np_min), "off", params$np_min)`; duplicate-name check `r ifelse(params$check_duplicate_readnames, "on", "off")`; downsampling `r ifelse(is.na(params$downsample), "off", format(params$downsample, big.mark = ","))`; adapter trimming `r ifelse(params$trim, "on", "off")`.

---

# Sequencing files

```{r file_discovery}
if (redraw) file_details <- m1$file_details else {
file_paths <- list.files(params$dir_data, full.names = TRUE, recursive = params$import_recursive,
                         pattern = paste(params$import_patterns, collapse = "|"))
if (!length(file_paths)) stop("No sequencing files found in ", params$dir_data)
file_names <- basename(file_paths)
gz <- grepl("\\.gz$", file_names)
file_formats <- ifelse(gz, paste0(tools::file_ext(sub("\\.gz$", "", file_names)), ".gz"), tools::file_ext(file_names))
file_stems <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(sub("\\.gz$", "", file_names))
file_details <- data.frame(file_name = file_names, file_stem = file_stems, file_format = file_formats,
                           file_path = file_paths, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(paired_direction = dplyr::case_when(grepl(params$r1_pattern, file_name) ~ "R1",
                                      grepl(params$r2_pattern, file_name) ~ "R2", TRUE ~ NA_character_),
         include = is.na(paired_direction) | params$select_one_of_pair == "all" | paired_direction == params$select_one_of_pair)
}
if (any(duplicated(file_details$file_stem[file_details$include])))
  stop("Two input files share a file stem: ", paste(unique(file_details$file_stem[duplicated(file_details$file_stem)]), collapse = ", "))
file_stem_vector <- setNames(file_details$file_stem[file_details$include], file_details$file_stem[file_details$include])
dt_compact(as.data.frame(table(format = file_details$file_format[file_details$include])), caption = "Files imported, by format")
```

```{r file_table}
dt_full(file_details, caption = "All files found (include = FALSE are the unused direction of paired-end reads)")
```

```{r import}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
if (redraw) { seq <- m1$sequences; stage_counts <- m1$stage_counts } else {
seq <- apply_fn(file_stem_vector, function(fs) {
  i <- match(fs, file_details$file_stem)
  import_sequencing(file_details$file_path[i], file_details$file_format[i])
})
stage_counts <- data.frame(file_stem = names(seq), imported = vapply(seq, length, integer(1)))
}
timings[if (redraw) "Loading the saved results" else "Import"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

---

# PacBio HiFi metrics

PacBio HiFi BAMs are detected per sample from the `np` tag (falling back to `@PG` lines naming ccs, skera or lima), so mixed cohorts are handled. **np** is the number of polymerase passes behind a HiFi read and **rq** its predicted accuracy (HiFi reads have rq ≥ 0.99). The section is skipped when no PacBio BAMs are present.

```{r pacbio_detect}
if (redraw) { is_pacbio <- m1$is_pacbio; read_metadata <- m1$read_metadata; pacbio_summary <- m1$pacbio_summary; any_pacbio <- any(is_pacbio) } else {
is_pacbio <- vapply(file_stem_vector, function(fs) {
  i <- match(fs, file_details$file_stem); detect_pacbio(file_details$file_path[i], file_details$file_format[i])
}, logical(1))
any_pacbio <- any(is_pacbio)
read_metadata <- NULL; pacbio_summary <- NULL
if (any_pacbio) {
  .t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
  # Tags were read with the sequences (bam_import); re-read only if they are missing
  read_metadata <- lapply(setNames(names(file_stem_vector)[is_pacbio], names(file_stem_vector)[is_pacbio]), function(fs) {
    md <- S4Vectors::metadata(seq[[fs]])$bam_tags
    if (is.null(md)) md <- extract_pacbio_metadata(file_details$file_path[match(fs, file_details$file_stem)])
    md
  })
  if (!is.na(params$np_min)) {
    for (fs in names(read_metadata)) {
      keep <- read_metadata[[fs]]$read_name[!is.na(read_metadata[[fs]]$np) & read_metadata[[fs]]$np >= params$np_min]
      seq[[fs]] <- seq[[fs]][names(seq[[fs]]) %in% keep]
      read_metadata[[fs]] <- read_metadata[[fs]][read_metadata[[fs]]$read_name %in% keep, ]
    }
  }
  pacbio_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(read_metadata), function(fs) {
    md <- read_metadata[[fs]]
    data.frame(file_stem = fs, n_reads = nrow(md), median_np = median(md$np, na.rm = TRUE), mean_np = mean(md$np, na.rm = TRUE),
               median_rq = median(md$rq, na.rm = TRUE), mean_rq = mean(md$rq, na.rm = TRUE),
               median_qv = rq_to_qv(median(md$rq, na.rm = TRUE)))
  }))
  timings["PacBio metrics"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
}
# The tags are now in read_metadata; drop the copies held with the sequences
for (fs in names(seq)) if (!is.null(S4Vectors::metadata(seq[[fs]])$bam_tags)) S4Vectors::metadata(seq[[fs]])$bam_tags <- NULL
stage_counts$after_np_filter <- vapply(seq[stage_counts$file_stem], length, integer(1))
}
cat(sprintf("%d of %d samples are PacBio HiFi BAMs.%s", sum(is_pacbio), length(is_pacbio),
            if (!is.na(params$np_min)) sprintf(" Reads with np < %d removed.", params$np_min) else ""))
```

## Pass count and read quality per sample

Each point is one sample's median pass count (left) or median read quality (right) across its reads; the box shows the spread across samples and the red diamond and label give the cohort mean. Read quality is shown as a Phred-scaled QV, –10 × log10(1 – rq), so that the differences between HiFi reads are visible: rq 0.99 is QV 20, rq 0.999 is QV 30 and rq 0.9999 is QV 40 (capped at 60, PacBio's maximum). Samples well below the others had fewer passes, and so less accurate consensus reads.

```{r pacbio_plots, eval=any_pacbio, fig.height=5}
pb_long <- pacbio_summary %>% dplyr::select(file_stem, `Median pass count (np)` = median_np, `Median read quality (QV)` = median_qv) %>%
  pivot_longer(-file_stem, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")
p_pacbio <- ggplot(pb_long, aes(x = "", y = value)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_y") + expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Per-sample median", title = "PacBio HiFi pass count and read quality",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d PacBio samples; one point per sample; axes from 0, so that small differences are not magnified", nrow(pacbio_summary))) +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
print(p_pacbio)
save_plot(p_pacbio, file.path(plots_dir, "pacbio_np_rq.png"), 10, 5)
```

## Pass count

**np** is the number of times the polymerase went round the circular molecule; the HiFi read is the consensus of those passes, so more passes give a more accurate read. PacBio reports np only up to a cap (on Revio, 60): a read with 60 or more passes is reported as 60, so the reads at the cap form a single bar, not a real peak.

```{r pacbio_np_setup, eval=any_pacbio}
np_len <- rbindlist(lapply(names(read_metadata), function(fs) {
  md <- read_metadata[[fs]]
  data.table(np = md$np[match(names(seq[[fs]]), md$read_name)], read_length = width(seq[[fs]]), file_stem = fs)
}))[!is.na(np)]
np_max <- max(np_len$np); at_max <- mean(np_len$np == np_max)
# Kinnex (skera) reads are segments of one long concatenated HiFi read, and every segment
# carries the pass count of that whole read, so np says nothing about the segment's own length
# (skera names each segment <movie>/<zmw>/ccs/<start>_<end>, the position within the long read)
seg_share <- mean(grepl("/ccs(/[a-z]+)?/[0-9]+_[0-9]+$", unlist(lapply(seq, names), use.names = FALSE)))
# (or, failing that, the files are named as skera output)
segmented <- seg_share > 0.5 || all(grepl("skera", file_details$file_name[file_details$include], ignore.case = TRUE))
```

`r if (any_pacbio && segmented) sprintf("**These reads are Kinnex (skera) segments.** They were cut from longer concatenated HiFi reads (%s of the read names give the segment's position in its long read), and each segment carries the pass count of the whole concatenated read. np therefore depends on how long the array was, not on the length of the amplicon, and short and long reads are expected to have the same pass counts.", percent(seg_share, 1)) else ""`

### Pass count distribution

**How to read this.** Every read, all samples pooled: the grey bars are the share of reads with each pass count, and the orange bar at `r if (any_pacbio) np_max else "the cap"` holds every read with that many passes or more. The two lines split the reads at the median read length into shorter and longer reads, each scaled to its own total, so a difference in pass count between short and long reads (for example between the normal and the expanded allele) shows as a gap between the lines.

```{r pacbio_np_hist, eval=any_pacbio, fig.height=5}
# Reads shorter and longer than the median read length (a split at the median keeps every read
# in one half, even when most reads share one length)
cut_len <- stats::median(np_len$read_length)
np_len[, third := data.table::fifelse(read_length <= cut_len, "short", "long")]
if (uniqueN(np_len$third) < 2) np_len[, third := data.table::fifelse(read_length < cut_len, "short", "long")]
lab_short <- sprintf("Shorter reads (up to %s bp)", comma(max(np_len[third == "short", read_length])))
lab_long <- sprintf("Longer reads (%s bp and over)", comma(min(np_len[third == "long", read_length])))
h_all <- np_len[, .N, by = np][, share := N / sum(N)][order(np)][, cap := np == np_max]
h_thr <- np_len[, .N, by = .(third, np)][, share := N / sum(N), by = third][order(third, np)]
h_thr[, third := factor(ifelse(third == "short", lab_short, lab_long), levels = c(lab_short, lab_long))]
med <- np_len[, .(m = as.numeric(stats::median(np))), by = third]
p_np_h <- ggplot(h_all, aes(np, share)) + geom_col(aes(fill = cap), width = 0.9) +
  geom_step(data = h_thr, aes(colour = third), direction = "mid", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_text(data = h_all[cap == TRUE], aes(label = sprintf("%s of reads at %d\n(%d or more passes)", percent(share, 0.1), np_max, np_max)), hjust = 1.08, vjust = 1, size = 3.2, colour = "#d95f02", lineheight = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey70", `TRUE` = "#d95f02"), guide = "none") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = setNames(c("#1f78b4", "#6a3d9a"), c(lab_short, lab_long)), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, np_max, 5), expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Pass count (np)", y = "Share of reads", title = "PacBio pass count, every read",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s reads, all samples; median %s passes (shorter reads %s, longer reads %s); %s at the cap of %d\nLines: the reads shorter and longer than the median read length, each as a share of its own reads",
                          comma(nrow(np_len)), stats::median(np_len$np), med[third == "short", m], med[third == "long", m], percent(at_max, 0.1), np_max)) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p_np_h); save_plot(p_np_h, file.path(plots_dir, "pacbio_np_distribution.png"), 10, 5)
```

### Pass count against read length

**How to read this.** The x-axis is the read length, in bands of a few bases. **Top:** how many reads fall in each band (log scale). **Middle:** the spread of pass counts within each band: the line is the median read, the dark band the middle 50% of reads and the light band the middle 80%; a band reaching the dashed line at `r if (any_pacbio) np_max else "the cap"` holds reads at the cap. **Bottom:** the share of each band's reads at the cap. Bands with fewer than 100 reads are left out. The shortest and longest 0.5% of reads are not drawn, so a few stray lengths do not stretch the axis.

**What it shows.** Whether longer reads got fewer passes. For a single amplicon per HiFi read, fewer passes fit in the run time for a longer insert, so the median and the share at the cap fall with length, and the expanded allele is read less accurately than the normal one. `r if (any_pacbio && segmented) "For Kinnex segments (as here) the lines should be flat, because every segment carries the pass count of the whole concatenated read." else ""`

```{r pacbio_np_length, eval=any_pacbio, fig.height=7}
xr <- stats::quantile(np_len$read_length, c(0.005, 0.995))
bw <- max(1, signif(diff(xr) / 100, 1))
n_np_all <- nrow(np_len)
np_in <- np_len[read_length >= xr[1] & read_length <= xr[2]][, len_bin := floor(read_length / bw) * bw + bw / 2]
np_q <- np_in[, .(n = .N, q10 = as.numeric(stats::quantile(np, 0.1)), q25 = as.numeric(stats::quantile(np, 0.25)), med = as.numeric(stats::median(np)),
                  q75 = as.numeric(stats::quantile(np, 0.75)), q90 = as.numeric(stats::quantile(np, 0.9)), cap = mean(np == np_max)), by = len_bin][order(len_bin)]
# Bands with too few reads are drawn as gaps, so lines do not join distant lengths
np_q <- np_q[data.table(len_bin = seq(min(np_q$len_bin), max(np_q$len_bin), by = bw)), on = "len_bin"]
np_q[is.na(n) | n < 100, c("q10", "q25", "med", "q75", "q90", "cap") := NA_real_]
# The axis covers the bands with enough reads to draw
x_lim <- range(np_q[!is.na(med), len_bin]) + c(-bw, bw) / 2
np_q <- np_q[len_bin >= x_lim[1] & len_bin <= x_lim[2]]
x_brk <- scales::breaks_pretty(n = 15)(x_lim)
x_scale <- function(lab = TRUE) scale_x_continuous(limits = x_lim, breaks = x_brk, labels = if (lab) comma else NULL, expand = c(0, 0))
p_np_top <- ggplot(np_q[!is.na(n) & n > 0], aes(len_bin, n)) + geom_col(width = bw, fill = "grey50") + x_scale(FALSE) + scale_y_log10(labels = comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads\n(log)") + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
p_np_mid <- ggplot(np_q, aes(len_bin)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q10, ymax = q90), fill = "#cce6e8") + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75), fill = "#80c1c7") +
  geom_line(aes(y = med), colour = "#00838f", linewidth = 0.8) + geom_point(aes(y = med), colour = "#00838f", size = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = np_max, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#d95f02") +
  annotate("text", x = x_lim[2], y = np_max, label = sprintf("cap: %d or more passes", np_max), hjust = 1.02, vjust = -0.4, size = 3, colour = "#d95f02") +
  x_scale(FALSE) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, np_max * 1.08), breaks = seq(0, np_max, 10)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pass count (np)\nline = median; bands = middle\n50% and 80% of reads") + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
p_np_cap <- ggplot(np_q, aes(len_bin, cap)) + geom_line(colour = "#d95f02", linewidth = 0.7) +
  x_scale(TRUE) + scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Read length (bp)", y = sprintf("Reads at\nthe cap (%d)", np_max)) + theme_bw() + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
p_np_len <- patchwork::wrap_plots(p_np_top, p_np_mid, p_np_cap, ncol = 1, heights = c(1, 3, 1.1)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(title = "PacBio pass count against read length",
    subtitle = sprintf("%s of %s reads; length bands %s bp wide\nThe shortest and longest 0.5%% of reads, and bands with under 100 reads, are not drawn%s",
                       comma(nrow(np_in)), comma(n_np_all), comma(bw), if (segmented) "\nKinnex (skera) segments: each carries the pass count of its whole concatenated read" else ""))
print(p_np_len)
save_plot(p_np_len, file.path(plots_dir, "pacbio_np_vs_length.png"), 10, 7)
np_tab <- np_in[, .(reads = .N), by = .(len_bin, np)][, share := reads / sum(reads), by = len_bin]
fwrite(np_tab[order(len_bin, np)], file.path(dirname(plots_dir), "pacbio_np_by_length.tsv"), sep = "\t")
rm(np_len, np_in); invisible(gc())
```

# Optional filters

```{r dedup}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
dup_summary <- NULL
if (redraw) {
  dup_summary <- m1$duplicate_summary
  if (params$check_duplicate_readnames) cat(sprintf("Duplicate read names: %s reads removed across the cohort.\n", comma(sum(stage_counts$after_np_filter) - sum(stage_counts$after_dedup))))
  else cat("Duplicate read-name check off (check_duplicate_readnames = FALSE).\n")
  cat(if (!is.na(params$downsample)) sprintf("Downsampled to at most %s reads per sample.\n", comma(params$downsample)) else "Downsampling off.\n")
} else {
if (params$check_duplicate_readnames) {
  res <- apply_fn(seq, select_longest_duplicate_readname)
  dup_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(res), function(fs) data.frame(file_stem = fs, duplicated_names = sum(res[[fs]]$read_name_count$count > 1))))
  seq <- lapply(res, `[[`, "dna_stringset"); rm(res)
  cat(sprintf("Duplicate read names: %s reads removed across the cohort.\n",
              comma(sum(stage_counts$after_np_filter) - sum(vapply(seq, length, integer(1))))))
} else cat("Duplicate read-name check off (check_duplicate_readnames = FALSE).\n")
stage_counts$after_dedup <- vapply(seq[stage_counts$file_stem], length, integer(1))
if (!is.na(params$downsample)) {
  seq <- lapply(seq, downsample, sample_size = params$downsample)
  cat(sprintf("Downsampled to at most %s reads per sample.\n", comma(params$downsample)))
} else cat("Downsampling off.\n")
stage_counts$after_downsample <- vapply(seq[stage_counts$file_stem], length, integer(1))
}
timings["Duplicate names and downsampling"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

```{r trim}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
trim_summary <- NULL
if (redraw) {
  trim_summary <- m1$trim_summary
  cat(if (params$trim) sprintf("Adapter trimming: %s reads trimmed in total.\n", comma(sum(trim_summary$reads_trimmed))) else "Adapter trimming off (trim = FALSE).\n")
} else if (params$trim) {
  if (is.na(params$path_trim_patterns)) stop("trim = TRUE needs path_trim_patterns")
  ad <- read.csv(params$path_trim_patterns, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  pats <- setNames(ad$adapter_sequence, ad$adapter_name)
  pats <- c(pats, setNames(as.character(reverseComplement(DNAStringSet(pats))), paste0(names(pats), "_rc")))
  trim_one <- function(x) {
    before <- width(x)
    for (pt in pats) x <- trimLRPatterns(Lpattern = pt, Rpattern = pt, subject = x,
                                         max.Lmismatch = params$trim_max_mismatch, max.Rmismatch = params$trim_max_mismatch,
                                         with.Lindels = params$trim_with_indels, with.Rindels = params$trim_with_indels)
    list(seq = x, trimmed = sum(width(x) < before), bases = sum(before - width(x)))
  }
  tr <- apply_fn(seq, trim_one)
  trim_summary <- data.frame(file_stem = names(tr), reads_trimmed = vapply(tr, `[[`, 0L, "trimmed"),
                             bases_removed = vapply(tr, function(z) as.numeric(z$bases), 0))
  seq <- lapply(tr, `[[`, "seq"); rm(tr)
  trim_summary$pct_trimmed <- trim_summary$reads_trimmed / stage_counts$after_downsample[match(trim_summary$file_stem, stage_counts$file_stem)]
  cat(sprintf("Adapter trimming: %s reads trimmed in total.\n", comma(sum(trim_summary$reads_trimmed))))
} else cat("Adapter trimming off (trim = FALSE).\n")
timings["Adapter trimming"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

```{r trim_plot, eval=params$trim, fig.height=5}
p_trim <- ggplot(trim_summary, aes(x = "", y = pct_trimmed)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(0.1)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads trimmed", title = "Proportion of reads with an adapter trimmed, per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_trim); save_plot(p_trim, file.path(plots_dir, "adapter_trimming.png"), 6, 5)
```

# Reads per sample

One row per sample, labelled, ordered from fewest to most reads, on a log scale: the blue point is the reads left after this module's filters, and where a filter removed reads a grey ring marks the number imported, joined by a line. The dashed line is the median of all samples. Samples at the bottom are the ones most likely to give noisy repeat-length distributions; the table below gives the count after every step.

```{r read_counts, fig.height=min(40, 2 + 0.14 * length(seq))}
stage_counts$final <- vapply(seq[stage_counts$file_stem], length, integer(1))
rc <- as.data.table(stage_counts)[order(final)]
rc[, label := factor(short_labels(file_stem)[file_stem], levels = unique(short_labels(file_stem)[file_stem]))]
lost <- rc[imported > final]
p_counts <- ggplot(rc, aes(y = label)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = median(rc$final), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30") +
  { if (nrow(lost)) geom_segment(data = lost, aes(x = pmax(final, 1), xend = imported, yend = label), colour = "grey70") } +
  { if (nrow(lost)) geom_point(data = lost, aes(x = imported), shape = 21, colour = "grey50", fill = "white", size = 1.8) } +
  geom_point(aes(x = pmax(final, 1)), colour = "#377eb8", size = 1.8) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma) +
  labs(x = "Reads (log scale)", y = NULL, title = "Reads per sample after import and QC",
       subtitle = sprintf("%d samples; %s reads in total; dashed line = median, %s%s", nrow(rc), comma(sum(rc$final)), comma(median(rc$final)),
                          if (nrow(lost)) "; grey ring = reads imported, before the filters" else "")) +
  theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = if (nrow(rc) > 80) 5 else 7), panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
print(p_counts); save_plot(p_counts, file.path(plots_dir, "reads_per_sample.png"), 8, min(40, 2 + 0.14 * nrow(rc)))
```

```{r stage_table}
dt_full(stage_counts, caption = "Reads per sample after each step (a step that is switched off leaves the count unchanged)")
```

# Read length and quality

```{r read_qc}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
qc_summary <- if (redraw) m1$qc_summary else dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(seq), function(fs) {
  x <- seq[[fs]]
  w <- width(x)
  q <- if (is(x, "QualityScaledXStringSet") && length(x)) alphabetScore(quality(x)) / pmax(w, 1) else rep(NA_real_, length(x))
  data.frame(file_stem = fs, read_count = length(x), median_length = if (length(w)) median(w) else NA, mean_length = if (length(w)) mean(w) else NA,
             p05_length = if (length(w)) quantile(w, 0.05) else NA, p95_length = if (length(w)) quantile(w, 0.95) else NA,
             mean_phred = if (length(q)) mean(q, na.rm = TRUE) else NA)
}))
if (!redraw && !is.null(pacbio_summary)) qc_summary <- dplyr::left_join(qc_summary, dplyr::select(pacbio_summary, -n_reads), by = "file_stem")
set.seed(123)
len_sample <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(seq), function(fs) { w <- width(seq[[fs]]); data.frame(file_stem = fs, length = if (length(w) > 2000) sample(w, 2000) else w) }))
timings["Read QC"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Read length distribution

Read lengths from up to 2,000 reads per sample, pooled, with the count axis on a log scale so that the smaller peaks are visible next to the largest. For an amplicon each allele gives its own peak, so heterozygous samples with an expanded allele show two peaks (the shorter allele usually dominates, because PCR favours shorter products); reads well outside them are primer dimers, truncated products or chimeras, which Module 2 removes if they do not span both flanks.

```{r length_hist, fig.height=5}
p_len <- ggplot(len_sample, aes(length)) + geom_histogram(bins = 150, fill = "#377eb8") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1, base = 10), breaks = c(0, 10^(0:7)), labels = comma) +
  labs(x = "Read length (bp)", y = "Reads (log scale)", title = "Read length, pooled across samples",
       subtitle = "Up to 2,000 reads per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_len); save_plot(p_len, file.path(plots_dir, "read_length_distribution.png"), 10, 5)
```

## Read length and base quality per sample

Each point is one sample: its mean read length against its mean base quality (Phred, per base), sized by read count. In a heterozygous amplicon the mean length rises with the share of reads from the longer allele, so this also shows how evenly the two alleles amplified (the median is usually the shorter allele's length in every sample, so it is listed in the table but not plotted). Phred scores are not stored for FASTA input, so the plot is empty for FASTA.

```{r qc_scatter, fig.height=5}
p_qc <- ggplot(qc_summary, aes(mean_length, mean_phred, size = read_count)) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.7) + scale_size_continuous(labels = comma, name = "Reads") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) + expand_limits(y = 0) +
  labs(x = "Mean read length (bp)", y = "Mean base quality (Phred)", title = "Read length against base quality, per sample",
       subtitle = "Quality axis from 0, so that small differences are not magnified") + theme_bw()
print(p_qc); save_plot(p_qc, file.path(plots_dir, "quality_vs_length.png"), 10, 5)
```

```{r qc_table}
dt_full(qc_summary, caption = "Read length and quality per sample", digits = 3)
```

# Save output

```{r save}
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "01_import_qc.RData")
if (redraw) { module1_output <- m1; rm(m1) } else {   # a redraw leaves the saved results as they are
module1_output <- list(sequences = seq, file_details = file_details, stage_counts = stage_counts, qc_summary = qc_summary,
                       is_pacbio = is_pacbio, read_metadata = read_metadata, pacbio_summary = pacbio_summary,
                       trim_summary = trim_summary, duplicate_summary = dup_summary, hash = params$module_hash)
dir.create(dirname(output_path), showWarnings = FALSE)
save(module1_output, file = output_path, compression_level = 1)   # level 1: several times faster to write than the default, files slightly larger
}
write_excel_function(list(file_details = file_details, stage_counts = stage_counts, qc_summary = qc_summary,
                          pacbio_summary = pacbio_summary, trim_summary = trim_summary), xlsx_path)
```

**`r length(seq)`** samples and **`r comma(sum(stage_counts$final))`** reads passed to Module 2.
